dedupe_keys.name: biennial sub metre tree canopy maps of the orlando metropolitan area 2013 2021

description: These maps show tree canopy across the Orlando metropolitan area every two years from 2013 to 2021 at sub-metre resolution, derived from National Agriculture Imagery Program aerial photographs. A hierarchical classification uses vegetation, water, texture and brightness indices and deals with sensor differences, shadows and changing acquisition times between years. About 3,600 ground-truth polygons were used to check the maps, with 78 to 89 percent accuracy in tree detection, better than existing products according to the authors. Coverage: the Orlando metropolitan area, Florida. Access: free download from Zenodo as one zip per year (about 190 to 420 MB each); the IDL code is on GitHub. Licence: CC BY 4.0. Caveats: aerial imagery dates vary between years, so some change reflects season and shadow; accuracy is lower in dense urban cores. Simulation uses are street and park shade inputs for urban heat and thermal comfort models, tree loss tracking against development, and green infrastructure scenarios. Related records: the Miami-Dade urban tree canopy statistics and i-Tree style canopy assessments.
